# fcoinman

A CLI tool for Linux server compromise detection.
Born from a real incident: Ubuntu server infected with XMRig cryptominer + Kaiten IRC bot via SSH brute force (password: "password").

## What it detects

- XMRig cryptominer (CPU/GPU at 100%, known mining pool connections, --donate-level in cmdline)
- Kaiten IRC bot (IRC connections on port 6667/6697, non-standard systemd services like socket.service)
- P2PInfect botnet (the #1 Linux SSH botnet as of 2025)
- Backdoor UID-0 accounts (/etc/passwd entries with uid=0 that are not root)
- SSH authorized_keys backdoors (root@root pattern)
- LD_PRELOAD rootkits (/etc/ld.so.preload non-empty)
- Suspicious kernel modules (/proc/modules)
- Recently modified systemd services with non-standard binary paths
- Cron-based persistence (Outlaw botnet pattern)
- Attacker-installed tools: masscan, hydra, ncrack, medusa
- Cleared/empty auth.log (evidence of log wiping)
- SSH brute force evidence in auth.log (>20 failures from single IP)
- Attack timeline reconstruction from auth.log and syslog
- ELF binary static analysis: hash matching, string extraction, strip detection

## When to use

User is experiencing one or more of:
- Server fans running louder than normal
- CPU or GPU usage unexpectedly high (check with `top`, `htop`, `nvidia-smi`)
- Unknown processes in `ps aux`
- Cannot log in with own password (attacker may have changed it)
- Suspicious entries in `systemctl list-units --type=service`
- auth.log shows many failed SSH attempts
- Server was recently exposed with weak SSH password

## Install (Ubuntu / Debian)

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RainyForest23/fcoinman/main/install.sh | sudo bash

## Usage

sudo fcoinman scan                     # Full scan — all 7 detectors
sudo fcoinman scan --json              # Machine-readable JSON output
sudo fcoinman logs                     # Attack timeline from auth.log
sudo fcoinman analyze /usr/bin/socket  # Analyze a specific binary
fcoinman check-ip 194.87.143.62        # Check if IP is a known mining pool

## Output format

Human-readable colored terminal output by default.
JSON mode (--json) produces structured output suitable for parsing by AI assistants,
automation scripts, and CI/CD pipelines.

JSON verdict field values: "LIKELY_COMPROMISED", "SUSPICIOUS", "CLEAN"

## Source and documentation
